newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Diesel rebounds on buying surge.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Diesel rebounds on buying surge.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps rebounded on Friday amid buying interest and expectations of large purchases of physical gas oil later this evening, brokers and traders said.
They said gas oil swaps started recovering late on Thursday from its low values early this week when it dipped below $25.00 for June and July and was testing the support on the physical market.
The recovery followed the purchase of 600,000 barrels by a Japanese trader on Thursday from three sellers.
A group of buyers, who have been active since early March, are expected to emerge on the physical market again this evening, with one broker expecting them to take up to eight cargoes.

The market expected sellers to offer physical cargoes up to $25.80-$26.00 per barrel with trades assessed to be in the range of $25.35-$25.45, up from Thursday's deals of $25.10-$25.35 for end-May to mid-June lifting, free-on-board basis.
Swaps gas oil for June was quoted at $25.50/$25.60 per barrel, up 50 cents from Thursday, while July was indicated at $25.10/$25.30, up 25-35 cents.
June swaps traded between $25.40 and $25.55, while July traded at $25.00.
Weaker sentiment on kerosene prices saw June regrade narrowing to between flat and 10 cents per barrel, from Thursday's 20/45 cents, with June bid at 50 cents from 60/80 cents.
Fuel oil was steady at $101/$102 per tonne for June amid little activity, while naphtha was almost unchanged at $21.75/$22.00 for June and July.
